academic.name: Academic
academic.definition: Institutions, funding structures and communication systems that produce, validate and transmit knowledge and credentials, including higher education and research enterprises.
inclusion: higher education institutions and credentialing systems
research institutions and R&D governance
academic labour structures
scholarly communication infrastructure
funding and evaluation systems

exclusion.text: personal beliefs not embedded in academic institutions

academic/credentialing-structures.name: Credentialing and evaluation structures
academic/credentialing-structures.definition: Systems that assess, validate and formally recognise academic achievement and research output.
inclusion: degree systems, accreditation bodies, peer review systems, rankings

academic/funding-structures.name: Funding and resource allocation structures
academic/funding-structures.definition: Systems that distribute financial and material resources within academia.
inclusion: grant agencies, funding councils, endowments

academic/higher-education-structures.name: Higher education structures
academic/higher-education-structures.definition: Organised institutions that deliver accredited education and formal qualifications.
inclusion: universities, colleges, degree-awarding bodies

academic/research-structures.name: Research structures
academic/research-structures.definition: Institutions and organisational units that produce new knowledge.
inclusion: research institutes, laboratories, R&D centres

academic/scholarly-communication-structu.name: Scholarly communication structures
academic/scholarly-communication-structu.definition: Infrastructure that disseminates and archives academic knowledge.
inclusion: journals, conferences, repositories, publishing platforms

economic.name: Economic
economic.definition: Production, distribution, exchange and accumulation structures through which scarce resources and goods and services are created and allocated across institutional units.
inclusion: production systems, and firms and households as producers within boundary
market exchange and price formation structures
distribution and redistribution mechanisms
the monetary and financial system as allocation infrastructure
accounting and measurement infrastructure representing economic activity

exclusion.text: unpaid domestic services outside the SNA production boundary
technological capability absent allocation or scarcity structures

healthcare.name: Healthcare
healthcare.definition: Organisations, people, infrastructures and governance arrangements whose primary intent is to promote, restore or maintain health, including the core system functions that deliver and finance care.
inclusion: care delivery infrastructure and pathways
workforce and professional regulation structures
financing and purchasing structures
governance and stewardship structures
supply systems for medicines and technologies integral to care

exclusion.text: biological mechanisms inside the human body
general social determinants where the primary intent is not health

human-biological.name: Human biological
human-biological.definition: The organised structures of the human organism, from cells to organ systems, and the stable functional organisation those structures enable, including the agreed terminologies that describe them.
inclusion: anatomical structures and their standardised nomenclature
cellular and molecular organisation directly constituting tissues and organs
organ-system architecture
reference-atlas representations of the body that preserve structural mapping

exclusion.text: technological tools used to measure or operate on biology
normative judgements about life and health

human-biological/nervous-system.name: Nervous system
human-biological/nervous-system.definition: The system responsible for information processing, signal transmission, and coordination of body functions.

legal.name: Legal
legal.definition: Institutionalised rule systems - sources of law, adjudication structures and enforcement mechanisms - that define rights and obligations and create binding decisions backed by legitimate authority.
inclusion: lawmaking sources such as statutes, delegated regulation and jurisprudence
adjudication institutions and compliance processes
legal enforcement mechanisms including sanctions, penalties and remedies
rights and obligations frameworks where legally constituted

exclusion.text: ethical judgements about what should be the case
informal social norms without formal enforceability
economic incentives absent a legal rule mechanism

meta.name: Meta
meta.definition: Formal organisation-of-knowledge structures - ontologies, top-level categories, representation standards and metadata or provenance systems - that define and relate concepts across domains to enable interoperability, retrieval, integration and analysis.
inclusion: ontologies, taxonomies and controlled vocabularies
metadata and provenance schemes
standards for semantic representation and exchange
top-level categories and mapping frameworks that mediate across domains

political.name: Political
political.definition: Institutions, authority relations and formal or informal decision structures that determine collective choices and the allocation of public power in a society.
inclusion: entities that hold or compete for legitimate coercive authority
entities that make or authorise binding collective decisions
structures of representation and participation
structures of accountability and oversight of state power

exclusion.text: courts and legislation analysed as legal structures

religious.name: Religious
religious.definition: Shared belief and practice complexes organised around sacred or ultimate concerns, including the institutions and community structures that maintain, transmit and regulate those beliefs and practices.
inclusion: belief and practice systems organised around sacred or ultimate concerns
religious institutions and leadership structures
ritual and community practices that reproduce the system
membership and affiliation structures, including non-theistic groups

exclusion.text: laws, rights and regulations governing religious practice
individual moral philosophy not embedded in a belief-practice community
political movements merely using religious rhetoric

technological.name: Technological
technological.definition: Artefacts, processes and infrastructures that apply organised knowledge to achieve practical objectives, including the standardised technical definitions and system components that enable design, deployment and operation.
inclusion: engineered artefacts and technical processes
technical infrastructures such as communications, compute, energy and manufacturing
standards and interoperability mechanisms
technology life-cycle structures treated as system components

exclusion.text: the scientific enterprise itself as a social institution
economic allocation and accounting as primary objects
